title: Haas reveal striking Godzilla-themed livery for Austin
excerpt:
Haas have presented a striking Godzilla-themed livery that will adorn the VF-26 cars of Ollie Bearman and Esteban Ocon at this weekend’s United States Grand Prix.

At the start of the year, Haas entered into a season-long collaboration with TOHO CO., LTD., the Japanese entertainment studio and home of fictional giant monster Godzilla.

Following on from an initial Godzilla livery at the Japanese Grand Prix, Haas have now put together a ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ design for the Austin weekend – one of three home races on the calendar for the team alongside Miami and Las Vegas.

While the previous Godzilla livery stuck to Haas’ core colour scheme of white, black and red, the latest creation – which celebrates the upcoming film release – brings in splashes of light blue and bold patterns.

title: Fornaroli set for McLaren FP1 runs after latest F1 test
excerpt:
Leonardo Fornaroli will return to the wheel of McLaren’s MCL40 over the coming weeks, with his next practice outings being planned for the Mexico City and São Paulo Grands Prix.

McLaren reserve driver Fornaroli made his first two FP1 appearances at the Barcelona-Catalunya and Hungary events earlier this season, meaning the young Italian will mark the team’s final two mandatory rookie sessions for 2026.

In preparation for those run-outs, Fornaroli – the 2024 F3 and 2025 F2 champion – joined McLaren’s Testing of Previous Cars (TPC) team at the Circuit Paul Ricard in France last weekend, where he completed almost 350 kilometres on the Grand Prix layout.

His sixth F1 test with the team, Fornaroli focused on longer runs (simulating FP1 sessions) and tried various set-ups aboard McLaren’s 2025 double championship-winning MCL39.

British racer Jake Hughes, who serves as a test and development driver for McLaren, also got some time in the MCL39 at Paul Ricard, continuing to provide him with a reference point for his simulator development work.

“I’m really excited to return to the MCL40 and do two more official Free Practice 1 sessions with the team,” said Fornaroli, who joined McLaren’s Driver Development Programme just under a year ago.

“The Mexico City and São Paulo Grands Prix are two great events, which will challenge me as a driver. Interlagos is a historic circuit with lots of mixed technical corners, and the altitude in Mexico City will definitely be a new physical challenge for me. It’s a great opportunity for my own development, and to also help the team over their weekend.

“This test at Circuit Paul Ricard was really beneficial. It’s been a few months since I was in an F1 car, so it was good to get back into it ahead of Mexico. This track is also really fun to drive, and of course driving the MCL39 for the first time made it even better. To drive a double championship-winning car was really cool.

“Thank you to the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team for giving me these opportunities, and to everyone in the McLaren Driver Development Programme for their guidance and continued support. I look forward to being back with the team in Mexico.”

McLaren have also announced that Fornaroli will race for their new Hypercar team in the World Endurance Championship (including the 24 Hours of Le Mans) in 2027, while continuing in his F1 reserve driver role.

title: What time is the 2026 United States GP and how can I watch it?
excerpt:
The 2026 Formula 1 season marches on with this weekend’s United States Grand Prix, which will see teams and drivers face the captivating challenge of the Circuit of The Americas.

Max Verstappen took Red Bull to new heights as he finally won the Singapore Grand Prix on his 10th attempt, improving to P4 in the Drivers’ Championship in the process. His comeback might not be enough to topple Kimi Antonelli – who now leads by 102 points and could theoretically clinch the title in Austin – but once the Dutchman gets into a rhythm, he’s tough to beat.

Head to the RACE HUB or scroll down for more on how and when you can watch the action, along with the global start times for each session.

What time is the 2026 United States Grand Prix?

The weekend will kick off with Free Practice 1 at 1230 local time on Friday, 23 October, followed by Free Practice 2 later that day at 1600.

A final hour of practice will begin at 1230 on Saturday, 24 October, before Qualifying gets underway at 1600. The Grand Prix itself will take place at 1500 on Sunday, 25 October.

Check out the image below to find all the global start times for Sunday’s race.

How can I watch the 2026 United States Grand Prix?

You can enjoy coverage from every session live on F1 TV Pro (available in selected countries), which brings fans closer to the action via exclusive features like onboard cameras on all 22 of the drivers’ cars, and access to both Pre-Race and Post-Race Shows.

F1 TV Pro can be streamed easily via Apple TV, Chromecast Generation 2 and above, Android TV, Google TV, Amazon Fire TV, and Roku. F1 TV Pro is free of ad breaks and available with commentary in six languages.

Fans can also watch via F1 TV Premium, a premier service that invites fans to step into the heart of the action with the ability to watch races in 4K Ultra HD/HDR on up to six different devices, as well as a personalised Multiview feature available on select devices with 26 different feeds to choose from.

Viewers can watch every F1 Grand Prix, F1 Sprint, Qualifying and practice session live in 4K Ultra HD/HDR at home, with F2, F3, F1 ACADEMY and Porsche Supercup sessions also available to watch live on the platform.

Alternatively, live timing will be available on F1.com and the F1 app across every session during the Grand Prix weekend.

Where is the 2026 United States Grand Prix taking place?

The Circuit of The Americas was officially opened in October 2012, with the 1978 World Champion Mario Andretti given the honour of completing the maiden lap in his title-winning Lotus 79.

It held its first Grand Prix just under a month later and Lewis Hamilton secured his last win for McLaren in front of a bustling crowd, establishing COTA as another enticing modern venue that quickly won fans over.

From the renowned Texan hospitality to the medley of corners borrowed from other tracks – watch out for the Maggotts/Becketts-esque run between Turns 3 and 6, and a replica of Hockenheim’s stadium section at Turns 12 through 15 – every aspect of COTA is full of character.

What is the weather forecast in the United States?

It’s expected to be a warm weekend in Austin, with temperatures peaking at 28 Celsius. There’s also a very low likelihood of rain, which should make it a comfortable event for drivers and fans alike.

When can I watch F1 ACADEMY during the 2026 United States Grand Prix weekend?

After a two-month break, F1 ACADEMY returns to COTA for the first time since 2023 for the penultimate round of the season, with Red Bull’s Alisha Palmowski looking to further extend her lead at the top of the standings.

A three-race format will be in place for the second time this year and will feature drivers tackling an Opening Race, Reverse Grid Race and Feature Race, delivering even more action as well as opportunities to score big.

Free Practice will start at 1225 local time on Thursday, 22 October before an all-important Qualifying session at 1630. The Opening Race, which uses drivers’ second-fastest Qualifying time to set the grid, will follow on Friday, 23 October at 1750, with the Reverse Grid Race taking place the next day at 1800.

Last but not least, the Feature Race will round out the weekend at 1200 on Sunday, 25 October.

title: 5 storylines we're excited about ahead of the United States GP
excerpt:
After a weekend off it’s time to get another triple header of races underway, and for the next leg we’re heading across the Atlantic Ocean to the United States. A new Drivers’ Champion could be crowned, but there are plenty of other exciting storylines as the paddock prepares to return to Austin for what is always a big weekend.

Antonelli’s first chance to become champion

It’s quite remarkable that Kimi Antonelli finds himself in this position in just his second season in Formula 1, but such has been his consistent form, the Italian could wrap up his first Drivers’ Championship as early as this weekend.

The permutations are simple when it comes to what Antonelli needs to do himself, and that’s win the race. Anything other than victory at Circuit of The Americas and the title celebrations will remain on hold for at least one more week, but if he is standing on the top step on Sunday afternoon then he will also need some other results to go his way.

Team mate George Russell is Antonelli’s nearest challenger, and the gap at present means Russell would need to finish no higher than ninth for Antonelli to become champion should he win. But even then there needs to be another result that goes in Antonelli’s favour, with Lewis Hamilton - currently third in the championship - coming home no higher than fifth in the United States Grand Prix.

It’s a long shot for it all to come together, but stranger things have happened.

Can Red Bull and Verstappen keep winning?

Antonelli acknowledged the recent form from Max Verstappen would make for a “very, very scary” scenario if the four-time World Champion was closer to him in the standings.

Verstappen has won each of the last two races – the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia as well as the Singapore Grand Prix – while also winning the Sprint in Singapore to secure a clean sweep. Add that to a tight second place in Baku, and Verstappen was just seven points away from a maximum score over the previous triple header.

The top 10 driver/team combination wins in F1 history

That run has lifted Verstappen up to fourth in the Drivers’ Championship, but at 119 points adrift he has to ensure Antonelli doesn’t outscore him by six points or more in order to keep his own extremely slim hopes alive.

What was impressive about the recent set of results is that they came on a variety of different tracks, including ones that Red Bull have been successful on in the past, but also ones where Verstappen had never won. The question now is whether that all-round performance can continue into the next set of races, making Verstappen a factor in the fight for victory at every round.

Upgrades still on the horizon

Despite his wins, one of the reasons Verstappen was not fully convinced he will be in the mix at the front for the remainder of the season is the development race.

2026 has seen a hugely exciting rate of development with the new cars, to such an extent that there have been major fluctuations in form at the front of the field. While Mercedes started off with a dominant car, Ferrari took the fight to them at the start of the European season, and then McLaren came on strong with a run of two wins and three pole positions in four races through late summer.

Now it is Red Bull’s turn to be the biggest threat, but will it remain that way? McLaren are planning on introducing further upgrades in Austin to build on a package that was brought to Baku, while other teams are also expected to continue developing their cars.

That’s because there is a lot to be learned for 2027 as well, and if a team have space in the budget cap to bring the developments to the car then they can get a clearer direction on where they are heading into next season.

Mercedes have not stated there will be new parts on their car in the United States, but they are looking forward to a race weekend with three practice sessions in which to try and understand the upgrade brought to Malaysia, after struggling to get the full performance out of it over the past two rounds.

The newest rookie on the F1 grid

Even without racing for a week, there has still been some big news coming out from one of the teams as Haas confirmed the latest addition to their driver line-up.

Formula 2 championship leader Rafael Camara will join Haas next year – agreeing a multi-year deal according to the team’s announcement – and is expected to form a partnership with Ollie Bearman in 2027. Camara has been hugely impressive in the junior categories, fighting with Antonelli in the Formula Regional European Championship in 2023, winning that title in 2024 and then following up with the Formula 3 crown a year later.

Camara on the 'crazy' achievement of joining Haas in 2027

An impressive outing during a testing of previous car (TPC) event in Portimao this summer sealed the deal for Camara, who has yet to appear during an FP1 session but showed the adaptability required to convince Haas he was the best candidate for the seat. He beat high quality opposition in the likes of Leonardo Fornaroli, Ryo Hirakawa and Jack Doohan to the drive, and will get his chance to show what he can do in a race seat next year.

With Haas Team Principal Ayao Komatsu suggesting it is a formality that Bearman is confirmed for another year, the news only leaves Racing Bulls with an official vacancy, as Alan Permane’s team have yet to confirm either of their drivers for 2027.

A huge crowd at a driver favourite

Almost every race weekend can be classified as a big event given the number of sell-out crowds seen this season, but a trip to Circuit of The Americas has regularly delivered one of the biggest attendances of the year in recent times.

Austin is a city that attracts a massive number of fans to join the party, with activations all across town to ensure there’s no chance of missing the fact that the race is happening. And it’s often an exciting race, with the track layout an all-round test for drivers, including significant elevation at Turn 1, high-speed changes of direction through the first sector, and good overtaking opportunities.

Strategy is not always clear-cut, either, so we’ve had a number of tense finishes in recent years as drivers converge late in the race.

And while we’ll celebrate the size of the visit to Texas this weekend, it will also provide the first opportunity to get the drivers’ reactions to the latest addition to the F1 calendar, following the announcement of the African Grand Prix in Rwanda last week.

title: How Verstappen fared in his Portimão GT outing
excerpt:
Max Verstappen and Valentino Rossi were both in action as the 2026 GT World Challenge Europe season reached its conclusion at the Autódromo Internacional do Algarve (Portimão) in Portugal.

With a short gap in the F1 calendar last weekend, Verstappen took the opportunity to represent his own Verstappen Racing team once more, following on from multiple outings over the last couple of years.

After their entry qualified 15th, Verstappen’s team mates Ben Barnicoat and Chris Lulham made solid progress over the first couple of stints, breaking into the top 10 and pushing towards a potential podium.

However, a penalty during Lulham’s stint left the #3 Mercedes-AMG GT3 machine down in 24th position when Verstappen took over the wheel, with a Safety Car period also hampering the Dutchman’s chances of a recovery.

When racing resumed, though, Verstappen displayed all the skills that have helped him become a four-time F1 World Champion – blending incredible raw speed with a series of bold overtakes to go from outside the top 20 to ninth by the chequered flag.

Team WRT’s Rossi had hoped to be in the mix with Verstappen through Qualifying – GT World Challenge Europe’s format featuring three segments (one for each driver), with the aggregate time for each car setting the grid.

However, Rossi’s efforts were undone by a track limits penalty, which cost the seven-time MotoGP champion and his squad a lap time in the second segment, and left them back in 60th on a 61-strong grid.

On race day, with 52 entries making the finish, and nine retiring across some three hours of racing, the #46 BMW M4 GT3 classified in 50th position.

Given the extra attention brought by Verstappen’s latest outing, GT World Challenge subsequently reported a record 9.7 million views of their live coverage on YouTube, as well as an on-site attendance of 28,000 people.

F1 will return to Portimão in 2027 as part of a two-year agreement confirmed at the end of last year.

title: 6 times drivers improvised after losing radio during a race
excerpt:
Max Verstappen might have sealed a dominant victory at the Singapore Grand Prix last weekend, but his race was not entirely without hiccups – the four-time World Champion having suffered issues with his radio during the event.

While Verstappen could hear his Race Engineer Gianpiero Lambiase, the Dutchman’s responses were inaudible – leading to some creative solutions from Lambiase, who developed a code of sorts by asking yes/no questions where Verstappen either had to stay silent or respond with a button press. The Red Bull team also made use of pit boards to communicate with their driver.

Verstappen is not the only driver to experience this kind of problem during a race, with several other well-known names facing radio glitches in the past – sometimes with very interesting consequences…

Sebastian Vettel and Mark Webber, 2012 Malaysian Grand Prix

While only one of Red Bull’s cars appeared to be suffering radio issues at Marina Bay in 2026, the team have previously seen this affect both sides of the garage – as was the case in the rain-affected 2012 Malaysian Grand Prix.

After the race was suspended due to heavy downpours, it soon became apparent when the action resumed that Sebastian Vettel and Mark Webber were experiencing communications problems. Initially this did not seem to be hampering Vettel too much, who was running in fourth while relying on the pit board.

However, after a late-race collision with Narain Karthikeyan while lapping the HRT, the team tried to call Vettel in for safety reasons – only for him not to hear the message. The German still managed to get his car over the line in P11, but conceded that losing radio had made the Grand Prix “very difficult”.

As for Webber, a fourth-place finish was a solid result on such a tough day yet it was not without its frustrations, the Australian admitting that he had resorted to tearing the radio out of his helmet due to the loud static becoming a distraction in already challenging conditions.

Michael Schumacher, 1999 French Grand Prix

Michael Schumacher made a number of memorable overtakes during his hugely successful F1 career – but it was some moves of a different kind from the German that caught the eye when disaster struck at the French Grand Prix in 1999.

In a rain-hit encounter at the Magny-Cours Circuit, Schumacher was looking to add further points to his tally as he battled reigning champion Mika Hakkinen for the title. That goal hit a snag, though, when the Ferrari lost communication with the pit wall.

Some quick-thinking from Schumacher resulted in a resolution of sorts, however, as the then-two time World Champion started to use hand signals towards his onboard camera to communicate with the team – given that he could be seen but not heard.

While this could not prevent him from ultimately ending the race back in fifth following a slow pit stop, it was certainly a noteworthy response to the radio problems.

Alex Albon, 2025 Las Vegas Grand Prix

For many drivers, losing communication during a race can be a hugely frustrating – and potentially result-affecting – occurrence. However, it seems that there can be some silver linings...

Alex Albon spent much of the 2025 Las Vegas Grand Prix without functioning radio after losing connection on his laps to the grid, leading him to quip afterwards that it was “pretty peaceful out there”.

On a more serious note, though, the Williams driver admitted that this had left him in the dark about how much damage he might be carrying following an incident at the start of the race, with communication limited to the pit boards.

Albon ultimately retired from the event rather than risk continuing due to the threat of safety issues, highlighting just how vital radio messages can be during a Grand Prix.

Max Verstappen, 2021 French Grand Prix

Verstappen’s success in Singapore despite his communication difficulties was impressive – and it appears to be an area that the Dutchman has form in.

Back in 2021, Verstappen was locked in a famously tense title fight with Lewis Hamilton and the Mercedes team. The Red Bull man held the lead in the standings when the paddock headed to Paul Ricard for the seventh round of the campaign, the French Grand Prix.

A two-stop strategy helped Verstappen to overtake Hamilton for the lead with just two laps remaining, giving the former his third victory of the season – despite the fact that, like in Singapore, a radio problem in the latter stages meant that he could receive his team’s messages but they could not hear him.

While Lambiase had advised him to try moving the microphone when convenient, the gremlins remained until the chequered flag – but the Dutch driver later played down the impact of the issue, given that it had only occurred after he had completed his pit stops.

Charles Leclerc, 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix

Although some drivers appear to take radio glitches in their stride, the problem is undoubtedly difficult and can lead to frustrations boiling over – particularly when coupled with other issues, as Charles Leclerc discovered at the Hungarian Grand Prix in 2023.

It was not the Monegasque’s day at the Hungaroring, where he experienced everything from his drinks tube being too short – meaning that he had no water during the race – through to a slow pit stop and then a five-second time penalty for speeding in the pit lane.

On top of this, Leclerc – who ended the event in P7 – suggested later on that struggles with the radio had been one of his key gripes during the race, explaining: “One out of four words is not understood by my engineer, because there's just problems with our radios in three, four races.

“So we need to fix that. And obviously my tone of voice is quite high because I need to make myself heard.”

Lewis Hamilton and Valtteri Bottas, 2017 Hungarian Grand Prix

As mentioned earlier, Red Bull know what it is like for both cars to lose transmission – and the same can be said for Mercedes, whose radio issues came at a crucial time in their fight for both titles back in 2017.

While the Ferraris of Sebastian Vettel – who led the championship by one point from Hamilton at that stage – and Kimi Raikkonen held first and second positions during the Hungarian Grand Prix, Valtteri Bottas was running in third ahead of team mate Hamilton.

The decision was made to invert the cars in order for Hamilton – who looked to have more pace – to attempt to chase after the Scuderia machines. However, radio issues were affecting both Silver Arrows cars, with Team Principal Toto Wolff later explaining that “our whole comms and data systems broke down” due to a crack in a fibre optic cable, leaving the squad to “fly blind”.

These problems particularly affected Hamilton and, while the Briton did overtake Bottas, he later honoured the plan to hand the position back if he was unable to pass Raikkonen. Hamilton conceded afterwards, though, that the swap could have been carried out sooner had it not been for the radio struggles.

This all resulted in Hamilton’s deficit to Vettel extending to 14 points, causing some concern for Mercedes at the time – but as we now know, a successful run for the British driver in the second half would see him clinch his fourth World Championship.

title: Colton Herta set for US debut in latest Cadillac F1 practice outing
excerpt:
Colton Herta is to complete his fourth FP1 session for Cadillac, and drive an F1 car in the United States for the first time at this weekend's Austin GP.

The reserve driver, who had already enjoyed outings in Barcelona, Hungary, and Italy will deputise for Sergio Perez in FP1 at Austin for his latest outing.

He will be the first American to drive in an official F1 session in the United States since Logan Sargeant finished 10th for Williams in 2023, and scored his only F1 point.

Herta has pedigree at Austin, and won his first IndyCar race at the track back in 2019 for Harding Steinbrenner Racing, before a second win later in the year at Laguna Seca.

"Driving the MAC-26 in front of the American fans at COTA is going to be special," he said.

"I have great memories at this track – winning my first IndyCar race here back in 2019 was a huge moment in my career, so stepping into an F1 car on this layout feels like coming full circle.

"I’ve built up a good rhythm with the team through my previous FP1 runs in Barcelona, Budapest, and Monza, so my goal for Friday morning is straightforward: execute the test program cleanly, help the engineers gather good data on the setup, and hand the car back to Checo with some useful feedback to support the team for the rest of the weekend."

title: Christian Horner declares true Liam Lawson stance after Red Bull axe
excerpt:
Christian Horner has said that he was "uncomfortable" with Red Bull's decision to promote Liam Lawson to the senior team at the start of 2025.

Following the disintegration of Sergio Perez's form after the second half of 2024, he was dropped for '25, with New Zealander Lawson drafted in as the Mexican's replacement alongside Max Verstappen.

However, Lawson had never enjoyed an F1 pre-season or started a season, and had just 11 grands prix to his name; nor had he ever raced at Australia's Albert Park or China's Shanghai circuits, the first two races of the season.

In Melbourne, Lawson suffered an engine problem and missed most of FP3 and qualified 18th before spinning out during the treacherous conditions in the uber-tricky-to-drive RB21, something even Verstappen was struggling with.

Next time out in China, Lawson was 20th on the grid, before climbing to 12th in the race, but before the Japanese GP at Suzuka, the decision was taken to send Lawson back to Racing Bulls and to promote Yuki Tsunoda to the senior team.

After his confidence had been "smashed", in Horner's words, Lawson recovered at Racing Bulls to finish 14th in the standings, including a career-best fifth place in Azerbaijan.

Reflecting on the episode in his new memoir Drive, a copy of which has been read by RacingNews365, Horner describes how he was "uncomfortable" with the decision to promote Lawson in the first place.

"Helmut [Marko] has championed the promotion, but I felt uncomfortable. He was young and inexperienced, with only 11 Formula 1 races to his name, and we would be asking a huge amount from him, and meanwhile, Helmut was playing games.

"Before the final race of the [2024] season in Abu Dhabi, he had informed Liam that he would be driving for Red Bull because of his influence. When I challenged Helmut on this, he typically denied everything.

"The move back to Racing Bulls was tough for Liam. But he really shouldn't have been promoted in the first place."

title: Oscar Piastri has 'no magic answers' to solve crucial McLaren question
excerpt:
Oscar Piastri believes there are "no magic answers" to solve the issues McLaren is facing with its MCL40 F1 car this season.

The reigning constructors' champions are currently third in the standings in 2026, and are just seven points ahead of a resurgent Red Bull, having also lost ground on Ferrari in second place over recent races.

McLaren last delivered a big upgrade at the Hungarian GP in July, with this initially prompting an upturn in form as Lando Norris won in both Hungary and the Netherlands before being denied a third win in four races in Spain due to an unluckily timed virtual safety car.

However, across the recent triple-header, McLaren slipped back to fourth-fastest behind Red Bull, Mercedes, and Ferrari, with Norris being very vocal that the car was tricky to drive and required immense input to get it to do what the drivers required around a lap.

Team boss Andrea Stella has promised that fresh upgrades are coming at the back end of the season in a bid to increase learning for the 2027 MCL41 machine, but in terms of finding instant solutions for the rest of 2026, Piastri feels there are "no magic answers."

"I think in the short term, it's probably as good as it's going to get," Piastri told media, including RacingNews365.

"But naturally, when you start giving yourself evidence of being able to drive a bit differently and in ways that aren't that natural, they slowly become more natural.

"So I think Malaysia was another good step forward in terms of understanding what I need to do and not having to work quite so hard to get there, and getting there a little bit more intuitively and without as much effort, which is ultimately the place I want to get to in this part of the year.

"And to fundamentally bring the car a bit closer to where I would like it to be, I don't think we're going to have any magic answers this year.

"The cars themselves are very different. The tyres are quite different as well, so that's not going to change anytime soon."

[Article continues below].

Piastri's own improvement

Addressing his own upturn in performance after a poor season in which he has not claimed a podium in 14 races since third in the Miami GP, Piastri pointed to his pace at certain points of the recent races in Baku and Sepang as evidence he was slowly making the progress required.

"But I definitely feel like the last two weekends [in Azerbaijan and Sepang], on a personal level, I've been performing much better," he added.

"In Baku, for the first stint of the race, I was very strong. The middle stint in Malaysia was very strong.

"So I feel like on a personal level, I'm definitely making progress. But it's still not as comfortable as I would like."

title: Will Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title in the United States GP?
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli heads to the United States Grand Prix in Austin this weekend with the opportunity to claim his first F1 world championship.

The Italian is 102 points clear of team-mate George Russell and 111 clear of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, with the magical number for Antonelli being a lead of 125 points after the weekend, when there will be just five races and 125 points left up for grabs.

For Antonelli to win the title in Austin, he must win the race for his part of the equation. If he does not win the United States GP, he cannot win the title in Austin.

Should Antonelli win, his lead over Russell would grow to 127 points and to 136 over Hamilton.

To keep their hopes alive, Russell would be required to finish eighth or higher and Hamilton fourth or higher if Antonelli wins.

If Antonelli wins, Russell is ninth or worse, and Hamilton is fifth or worse, the title will be Antonelli's - and crown him the youngest champion in F1 history.

If Antonelli's lead is exactly 125 points following the US Grand Prix, he will win the title on countback, as he will hold nine grand prix wins to Russell on three, who could then claim a maximum of eight should the Briton sweep the Mexico City, Sao Paulo, Las Vegas, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi races.

The number of wins is used as the first tiebreaker when championship points are level.

title: Toto Wolff takes blame for Lewis Hamilton-Nico Rosberg 'micromanagement'
excerpt:
Toto Wolff has admitted he was at fault for over-managing the 2016 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, the race that decided the title fight between Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg.

Hamilton led home Rosberg by 0.439 seconds at Yas Marina that day, but the German's second place was enough to clinch the drivers' championship by three points.

The result was overshadowed by Mercedes' attempts, via team radio, to get Hamilton to speed up and protect the race win from a fast-closing Sebastian Vettel, instructions Hamilton repeatedly ignored as he looked to back Rosberg into the chasing pack.

Ten years on, Mercedes team principal Wolff has conceded that the intervention from the pit wall was unnecessary and that experience would have told him to leave the drivers alone.

Speaking about the episode, Wolff said he would have approached the situation differently with the benefit of hindsight.

"Looking back, I wish I had had 10 years more experience than I have today," he said, speaking to the media, including RacingNews365.

"That's because there are a few things I would have handled differently, and maybe avoided some of the controversy.

"Particularly in the last race where we tried to micromanage a situation that didn't need to be managed, in my opinion, and that was my fault.

"So yes, 10 years! It's crazy how fast time runs. It feels like it's maybe five years ago, but we've moved on from that.

"My relationship and the team's relationship with Lewis is as strong as it can be whilst being rivals on track, and the same with Nico."

Wolff - 'You need to take your hat off'

Mercedes did not sanction Hamilton once Rosberg's retirement confirmed the title had been settled, and the team subsequently simplified its written "rules of engagement" between team-mates, having concluded that management should not have tried to alter the pace of a title-deciding finale.

Wolff also reflected on Rosberg's life since retiring from the sport immediately after claiming that 2016 title, pointing to the German's success as a venture capital investor.

"There are not many Formula 1 drivers, other than Niki [Lauda], who I know that have been able to kind of reinvent themselves in a totally different career," he said.

"And I see Nico a lot. I respect him a lot. We are friends. He set up a venture capital fund that is one of the best performing. He is giving it 24/7. He is very hard-working. He is respected within the tech industry very much.

"I am happy to be invested there and associated, and you really need to take your hat off, seeing what he's been able to achieve in this very short time of 10 years since he's left the sport."

title: Formula E CEO eager to explore potential Max Verstappen partnership
excerpt:
Formula E CEO Jeff Dodds has said he sees genuine potential for the electric series to work with Max Verstappen, both on track and through the Dutchman's wider business ventures.

Several Formula 1 drivers have taken a close look at Formula E's new Gen4 car this year, with the machine making its competitive debut in Season 13.

Lando Norris was among those to react positively after seeing the car during the Monaco E-Prix weekend, while Carlos Sainz and Nico Hulkenberg also inspected the vehicle in person.

The Gen4 package brings a significant step up in performance, with permanent all-wheel drive, race power rising to 450 kW and peak Attack Mode output reaching 600 kW. Development driver James Rossiter has likened the car's initial acceleration to that of Formula 1's V10 era machines of the early 2000s.

Dodds would like to see Verstappen get behind the wheel of the Gen4 car, even if no conversation about a test has taken place since the four-time world champion signed a new long-term deal with Red Bull.

Asked whether he had spoken to Verstappen further about the car, Dodds told RacingNews365 in a recent interview that the pair hadn't been in touch on the matter.

"No, we haven't talked to him more about the car," said Dodds. "I know he's very focused, delighted to see him re-sign with Red Bull for the long term.

"And obviously, we know the team there really well, and I think they're doing a really good job. But I'd still love to see Max in this car, partly because I just really value his insight.

"So I'd love him to drive the car to be able to give us real feedback, real insight into what he thinks of it."

"But I have no doubt that throughout this Gen4 era, we're going to be overwhelmed with potential new drivers."

Formula E eyes Max Verstappen possibilities

Formula E will race in the Netherlands for the first time next season, with Zandvoort hosting a double-header on June 18 and 19, 2027, as rounds 14 and 15 of the 2026/27 season.

Given Verstappen's commercial footprint extends well beyond his cockpit, with ventures spanning esports, GT racing and driver development through Verstappen Racing, Dodds believes there could be scope to involve him around the Dutch race weekend.

Asked if Verstappen could play a role in promoting the event, Dodds said the door remains open.

"Yeah, maybe," answered Dodds. "I forget what it's called, Verstappen Racing, but his investments are not just in him racing Formula 1 cars.

"He's also building academies, and he's very focused on sim-to-track activity. I think there are opportunities to do things with him that could be pretty exciting, but we haven't managed to have that conversation yet."

title: Ferrari hoping to steal crucial advantage on F1 rivals with major upgrade
excerpt:
Ferrari will introduce the latest evolution package on the SF-26 in Austin, with the aim of securing at least one more victory between now and the end of the season.

This is an evolution that has been planned for some time, not a “Plan B”, and is linked to performance issues that, following the introduction of the ADUO2-based Power Unit, have not met the Scuderia’s technical expectations.

In fact, it is an aerodynamic package that focuses on modifications to the underbody and the sidepod profiles, in part foreshadowing solutions that will, in fact, be part of the 2027 car.

In some respects, it seems appropriate to compare this development to the one recently introduced by Mercedes, though, in that case, it did not yield the results expected by the Brackley team’s engineers.

As for Ferrari, with six races remaining, it is fair to say that the car’s dynamic and aerodynamic characteristics are now well-established; therefore, the final development planned for the season cannot aim to radically overhaul the aerodynamic concept, but rather to reinforce its strengths while simultaneously seeking to broaden the car’s operating window.

What emerged from the last two races in Malaysia and Singapore was, in fact, that in terms of dynamics, the SF-26 responded consistently to the specific setups for the two tracks, effectively reducing the performance gap that still exists with the power unit.

At the same time, it was clear that while the balance achieved through a precise setup ultimately resulted in better tyre management, it could not, in fact, compensate on the straights for a lack of pure power.

The development to be introduced in Austin, as mentioned, will focus on an evolution of the underbody, which will allow not so much an increase in downforce but rather, based on the data collected, a different distribution of downforce: in short, a modification to the SF-26’s aerodynamic profile.

So far, and it’s worth reiterating, the SF-26 has proven to be one of the cars generating the most downforce this season, but with a characteristic that makes it virtually unbeatable in slow-speed sections, yet it is decidedly more vulnerable in fast corners.

It is for this reason that the performance seen at Sepang and Singapore served as further confirmation of these characteristics, which the team certainly does not want to lose with an eye toward 2027, but wishes to extend to the fast mixed-section stretches of the tracks, namely those layouts that make up the majority of the circuits on the calendar.

[Article continues below].

Ferrari's Austin upgrade could be delayed

At this point, it is still unclear whether all parts of this extensive package, which has been in development since before the summer break, can be implemented in Austin.

Specifically, it appears that the components related to the reshaping of the sidepods, in particular, may arrive at the last minute in Texas; as a result, their debut could be postponed by one week to Mexico.

In any case, it will be crucial to assess to what extent the modifications to the underbody alone are capable of meeting the goals that Ferrari’s aerodynamicists have set for themselves.

The SF-26 has not won since the British Grand Prix, a victory achieved in part due to a problem with the wheel shield on Kimi Antonelli’s Mercedes, but on that occasion, at a track that is very demanding from a dynamic standpoint, it had demonstrated that its overall performance was no fluke.

Since then, its rivals, first McLaren, then Red Bull, have proven more effective, preventing Ferrari from returning to victory.

Austin first and Mexico City next, with very different characteristics, particularly due to the extremely thin air in the latter, will serve as two crucial testing grounds to assess whether the latest direction in aerodynamic design, which forms the basis of the 2027 project, is the right one.

In Maranello, and among the fans as well, there is a strong hope that this will allow the team to start the season with greater confidence, but also to conclude the current one by demonstrating that the current concept has not yet reached its peak, even if it is nearing the limits of development.

title: F1 Middle East decision update as crucial US elections loom for Donald Trump
excerpt:
Formula 1's plans to end the 2026 season in the Middle East remain unchanged despite the United States issuing advisories for the region for citizens to consider contigency plans.

Over the weekend, US embassies and consulates in the region issued security updates, following recent attacks by Iranian-supported Houthis in Saudi Arabia, including attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which left 14 dead and hundreds injured.

According to the advisories issued across the Middle East and Persian Gulf, the "hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area."

However, as of the time of writing, the Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia have ceased.

A crucial point will come in early November when the United States holds its midterm congressional elections on Tuesday, November 3rd, with all 435 members of the House and one-third of the Senate up for re-election, in addition to numerous gubernatorial races across 36 of the 50 states.

The midterms are generally viewed as a referendum on the performance of the incumbent president and their party, with President Donald Trump and the Republicans currently holding both the White House and Congress.

Incumbent presidents generally fare badly in the midterms, with one example being in the 2010 midterms, when President Barack Obama's Democratic Party lost control of the House with huge losses whilst losing seats in the Senate.

President Trump faces growing unpopularity at home as the economy falters, fuel prices soar and the war in Iran drags on.

His approval rating is currently in the mid-30s, with the Republicans tipped to lose control of the House, and potentially the Senate in the midterms. However, Trump has confirmed that there will be no further US military strikes on Iran until after polling day.

"We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd," he wrote on his Truth Social page on October 8th.

In another important election, Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu is also going to the polls in the coming weeks, with voting day set for October 27th.

F1 is scheduled to host the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix on November 30th, and December 6th, respectively, to conclude the 2026 season, with earlier races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia postponed in April after the outbreak of hostilities between the United States, Israel, and Iran.

Bahrain was ultimately rearranged to Malaysia, with F1 intending to run a 23-race season, meaning Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, with RacingNews365 understanding that F1's travel plans are informed by the United Kingdom's Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office (FCDO).

Currently, as of October 19th, for both Qatar and the UAE, the FCDO states that British nationals in the Middle East should: "be prepared for possible flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions," and should keep up to date on travel arrangements and the latest news.

[Article continues below].

Imola back-up option continues

F1 has made clear that Imola will serve as a backup to Abu Dhabi should that race be unable to go ahead.

The Italian circuit stepped in at short notice to host a grand prix in the COVID-19-hit 2020 season, and joined the calendar through the first half of the decade under the 'Emilia Romagna Grand Prix' moniker, with the exception of the cancelled 2023 race due to floods.

Imola has been put on standby to step in for Abu Dhabi if required with work underway to prep in case the contingency is activated.

Due to be held on Abu Dhabi's date of December 6th, it would be the first European finish to an F1 season since 1997, when Jerez hosted the title showdown between Jacques Villeneuve and Michael Schumacher.

title: Kimi Antonelli shares 'open-minded' Mercedes desire in F1-title crunch time
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli would like to see Mercedes approach the United States Grand Prix with an open mind about set-up direction as the team continues to unlock the potential of its recent upgrade package.

Antonelli is on the cusp of his first F1 drivers' championship at just 20 years of age, and with five or six rounds of the campaign to go, he leads team-mate George Russell by 102 points in the standings.

Mercedes introduced a far-ranging upgrade package to the W17 at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, but the Brackley-based squad struggled to extract the expected level of performance from it.

It led the eight-time constructors' champion to conduct an A/B test at the Singapore Grand Prix, with Russell reverting to the previous specification car, which carried him to victory in the first round of that triple-header, in Baku.

Antonelli, who stayed with the updated package at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, explained the difficulties he experienced.

"The window is very small at the moment where the car operates and is very sensitive to the way you drive it, the way you take a corner, the way you brake," the eight-time grand prix winner told media, including RacingNews365. "So it reacts very differently.

"So hopefully now — in Austin, we have three free practices — we can be very open-minded with set-up, and hopefully we can find a way, and we can use the full potential of the package and finally see the gains."

High praise for an 'incredible job' by Mercedes

However, the Italian driver also expressed his confidence in the revised W17, despite the thin margins when it comes to optimising the set-up.

"But I think the team did an incredible job on just putting the car in a better place and allowing me to get the confidence.

"And now it's a starting point to keep working and keep extracting the potential."

title: McLaren confirm latest driver to ambitious new motorsport project
excerpt:
Leonardo Fornaroli has been confirmed as a McLaren Hypercar Team driver for 2027, with the reigning Formula 2 champion set to contest the World Endurance Championship alongside his existing duties as McLaren's Formula 1 reserve driver.

The 21-year-old Italian has enjoyed a rapid rise through the single-seater ranks, claiming back-to-back Formula 3 and Formula 2 titles in 2024 and 2025. Only four other drivers have managed that double, including McLaren's own Oscar Piastri.

That form earned Fornaroli a place on the McLaren driver development programme, through which he supported the McLaren F1 this year.

He will now add a Hypercar programme to his workload, racing the MCL-HY in the WEC from 2027 alongside Mikkel Jensen, Alex Lynn and 2024 WEC Drivers' Champion Laurens Vanthoor.

Fornaroli will continue in his reserve role for the F1 team at the same time next year, making him one of several young talents McLaren has fast-tracked across its driver pipeline as the WEC continues to attract rising single-seater stars.

Leonardo Fornali outlines 'huge honour' in McLaren WEC move

Speaking after the announcement, Fornaroli said joining the Hypercar project was a major step in his career.

"Joining the McLaren Hypercar Team is an incredibly exciting next step in my career and I'm grateful that my role as McLaren Formula 1 Reserve Driver has opened up this incredible opportunity," said Fornaroli.

"I'm delighted to be continuing in that role next year while also taking on this new challenge. To represent McLaren in the FIA World Endurance Championship and at the 24 Hours of Le Mans is a huge honour, and I am ready to give everything as we take on this new challenge together."

"I'd like to thank the McLaren driver development programme for supporting me throughout my journey and for giving me the opportunity to develop my skills on such a competitive and prestigious stage."

McLaren Hypercar team principal James Barclay, who previously worked with Fornaroli in Jaguar Formula E, praised the Italian's rapid progress through the junior categories.

"Leo is an exceptional talent: winning Formula 3 is a significant achievement, but to follow that by winning Formula 2 as a rookie underlines his natural talent and one of the most exciting drivers in motorsport," said Barclay.

"His speed, consistency and maturity at such a young age helped him achieve a huge amount in the junior categories and those same attributes make him an exciting addition to our McLaren Hypercar Team. We have a great driver line-up forming, which blends experienced sports car drivers and now young talent for our debut season.

"I worked with Leo briefly in my previous role and his approach and performance impressed me very much, we both look forward to taking on McLaren's debut season in the World Endurance Championship together."

title: Max Verstappen shares key differences between recent Red Bull transformations
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has pointed out some of the differences between Red Bull's late-season revival this season and last year, when a re-tooled RB21 helped vault him to within two points of a fifth consecutive F1 drivers' championship.

Verstappen has no hope of a similar turnaround this campaign, and will be officially ruled out of title contention if Kimi Antonelli outscores him by just six points in the upcoming United States Grand Prix.

However, the RB22's recent turnaround in fortunes is strikingly similar to the transformation its predecessor experienced at the Italian Grand Prix last September.

A floor upgrade at Monza headlined Red Bull managing to unlock the full potential of that car, which has previously proved troublesome and left him 104 points behind the then-leader in the championship, Oscar Piastri, heading into the round at the Temple of Speed.

This time around, Verstappen and the Milton Keynes-based squad were staring down the barrel of a first winless campaign since 2015, before an upgrade in Baku lifted the team into contention for victories on merit, across differing circuit profiles, as proved to be the case at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and at the Marina Bay Street Circuit in Singapore.

Asked how different the two transformations have been, and whether last year was more down to set-up and unlocking potential, whereas this season the resurgence has been the result of upgrades, Verstappen agreed.

"Yes, exactly. And you answered it yourself already," the Dutchman responded to media, including RacingNews365. "Two completely different cars as well, right, with the regulations.

"Also, two completely different problems that we had to find lap time [from]."

"Plus, of course, also this year with the engine side of things, I think for everyone it's been sometimes a bit complicated to get the most out of it."

[Article continues below]

Eliminating weaknesses

Last year, the RB21 had pace enough to win two of the opening seven rounds, but this year, its successor was over a second off the performance of Mercedes, which dominated the early stretch of the campaign.

Red Bull has progressed significantly in that time, both from the chassis and aerodynamic perspective, but also with its fledgling power unit, built in collaboration with Ford.

Nonetheless, Verstappen can still see considerable room for growth, and is keen to see steps taken heading into 2027.

"But from race one to now, I think we've gained a lot of experience," the four-time F1 drivers' champion added. "Of course, still not where we want to be, but I guess everyone will say the same thing.

"But we have learned so much and, definitely, also on the car side, have fixed a lot of our weaknesses. We just need to keep improving, keep learning this year, so that we can apply it into next year."

title: Fernando Alonso declares true Honda position ahead of F1 'question mark'
excerpt:
Fernando Alonso believes that Honda "deserves another opportunity" to produce a competitive F1 power unit with the changes coming in for 2027.

Honda's return to grand prix racing with Aston Martin in 2026 has been beset by numerous problems with its RA626H power unit, which initially started with severe vibrations in the early part of the season, which Adrian Newey claimed could leave Alonso and Lance Stroll with "severe nerve damage."

The issue was eventually fixed through countermeasures, with Honda delivering a new power unit through its first ADUO token at the Dutch GP, with its second one being used to introduce a new turbo for Stroll in Spain and then Alonso in Azerbaijan.

However, the unit has continued to struggle with turbo lag and drivability issues all season in the first year of the 50:50 split in terms of power output between the ICE and the 350kw battery systems.

For 2027, F1 will move away from this equal split, and by 2028, will reach a 60:40 split in favour of the ICE to generate power, with this being achieved by the increase of fuel flow.

Alonso will return for a 24th season of grand prix racing in 2027, and become the first 46-year-old to compete in a world championship grand prix since Maurice Trintignant at the 1964 French GP.

Looking ahead, Alonso felt that Honda had "started on the wrong foot" and deserved another chance to produce a competitive engine.

"I have no guarantees that 2027 will be more fun, but it is a commitment that you have to make with yourself, and at the end of the day, I feel fast, I feel motivated, I feel that I'm enjoying what I'm doing," Alonso told media, including RacingNews365.

"And if I'm sitting at home watching TV, watching races, I will feel that I can do better than them, you know. That's what I felt when I was away from F1, and I was watching races, and I was thinking: 'Wow, that was not right'.

"I was always feeling the fire inside of being there and trying to do better, and I still feel it now.

"As long as I have that inside, I think it's not time to stop. So yeah, the decision was more about the rules, and how enjoyable it is to drive these cars and these rules.

"I decided that maybe next year, with the 60-40 and with the second year of the rules, maybe there is a little bit of a better compromise on that, so let's do it one more time.

"Let's give Honda another opportunity, especially on the power unit side. We started on the wrong foot, and it is a question mark what is going to happen next year. But I think they deserve another opportunity, and I feel fast."
